title: CEFR Multilevel Mock - Speaking - Variant A (Everyday life, home and daily routine)

parts.title: Part 1.1
parts.instructions:
CEFR Multilevel Mock - Speaking - Variant A (Everyday life, home and daily routine) | Part 1.1

Part 1.1 - Exchanging personal information (Everyday life, home and daily routine). CEFR A1-A2. Three short questions about yourself and your interests, asked one after another. 30 seconds for each answer. NO preparation time. These are scored items 1, 2 and 3 (0-5 together).

questions.q:
[FULL MOCK - CEFR Multilevel Mock - Speaking - Variant A (Everyday life, home and daily routine)]
[Whole test: Part 1.1 (3 questions, 30 seconds each) - Part 1.2 (2 pictures; 45 + 30 + 30 seconds) - Part 2 (1 picture, 3 questions together; 1 minute preparation + 2 minutes) - Part 3 (topic statement with FOR and AGAINST lists; 1 minute preparation + 2 minutes). Eight scored items, maximum raw score 21, converted to a rating out of 75. Allow about 15 minutes in total, including the preamble below.]

EXAMINER PREAMBLE, before Part one, not scored:
"Good morning / Good afternoon. My name is your examiner today. Could you tell me your full name, please? Thank you. And could you show me your identity document, please? Thank you. This is the speaking test of the CEFR Multilevel mock. It has four parts and takes about fifteen minutes. Please answer in English. Are you ready?"

[Stage direction: write the candidate's name, the test name (CEFR Multilevel Speaking Mock A) and the start time on the mark sheet, check that the recorder is running, then begin Part one.]

[PART 1.1 - CEFR A1-A2 - scored items 1, 2 and 3 - theme: everyday life, home and daily routine]

EXAMINER, read aloud word for word:
"Part one. In this part, I am going to ask you three short questions about yourself and your interests. And then, you will see some photos and answer some questions about them. You will have 30 seconds to reply to each question. Begin speaking when you hear this sound (chime)."

[Stage direction: there is NO preparation time in this part. Ask the three questions one after another. Sound the chime before each question, start timing when the candidate begins, and stop the candidate politely when the 30 seconds are up. Do not comment on the answers and do not add extra questions of your own.]

QUESTION 1 (30 seconds) - "What time do you usually get up on a working day, and what is the first thing you do?"

QUESTION 2 (30 seconds) - "Tell me about the room in your home where you spend the most time."

QUESTION 3 (30 seconds) - "What do you usually do at home in the evening?"

[Stage direction: after the third answer, say "Thank you." and move straight on to Part 1.2.]
questions.topic: CEFR Multilevel Speaking Mock A - Part 1.1

parts.title: Part 1.2
parts.instructions:
CEFR Multilevel Mock - Speaking - Variant A (Everyday life, home and daily routine) | Part 1.2

Part 1.2 - Comparing two pictures and justifying an opinion (Two contrasting daily routines at home). CEFR B1. Three questions asked one after another: question 4 compares the two photographs (45 seconds), questions 5 and 6 are opinion questions (30 seconds each). NO preparation time. These are scored items 4, 5 and 6 (0-5 together).

questions.q:
[PART 1.2 - CEFR B1 - scored items 4, 5 and 6 - theme: two contrasting daily routines at home]

[Stage direction: show the candidate the two photographs side by side on the screen. If no photograph has been attached in Test bazasi, read the bracketed descriptions aloud slowly instead.]

[PICTURE 1: a man in his early thirties ironing a work shirt in a small, very tidy one-room flat at about seven in the morning; his phone is propped up against a mug playing something he is only half watching, a bowl of cereal stands unfinished on the worktop, and his coat and bag are already waiting by the door.]

[PICTURE 2: a large kitchen on a Sunday afternoon where a family of four are cooking together; flour is spread across the wooden table, two children are kneading dough with their sleeves rolled up, a grandmother is chopping vegetables and laughing, nobody looks in a hurry and the radio is on.]

EXAMINER, read aloud word for word:
"Now, I am going to ask you to compare two pictures and I will ask you two questions about them. Look at the photographs. What do you see in these pictures?"

QUESTION 4 (45 seconds) - the compare-and-describe question, exactly as read out above: "Look at the photographs. What do you see in these pictures?"
[Stage direction: no preparation time. Sound the chime, allow 45 seconds, and stop the candidate politely when the time is up. If the candidate describes only one photograph, you may prompt once: "And the other picture?"]

QUESTION 5 (30 seconds) - "Which of these two kinds of day would you prefer to have, and why?"

QUESTION 6 (30 seconds) - "Do you think everyone living in the same home should share the housework equally? Why, or why not?"

[Stage direction: questions 5 and 6 are asked one after another with no preparation time, 30 seconds each. Sound the chime before each one. After the third answer say "Thank you." and move on to Part two.]
questions.topic: CEFR Multilevel Speaking Mock A - Part 1.2

parts.title: Part 2
parts.instructions:
CEFR Multilevel Mock - Speaking - Variant A (Everyday life, home and daily routine) | Part 2

Part 2 - Reasoning on an abstract topic (How people organise their daily lives). CEFR B2. One picture and three questions presented at the same time. You do NOT need to describe the picture; it is there only to bring the theme to mind. 1 minute to prepare, then 2 minutes to answer all three questions together. This is scored item 7 (0-5).

questions.q:
[PART 2 - CEFR B2 - scored item 7 - an abstract angle on everyday life and daily routine]

[Stage direction: show the picture and the three questions on the screen AT THE SAME TIME. The candidate is NOT required to describe the picture - it is there only to bring the theme to mind. Give exactly 1 minute of preparation in silence, then sound the chime and allow 2 minutes for all three questions together. Do not interrupt between the questions.]

[PICTURE: a narrow galley kitchen at about seven in the morning with three adult housemates trying to use it at once - one waiting at the kettle, one reaching past him to open the fridge, a third eating toast standing up with his bag already on his shoulder; a handwritten cleaning rota is taped to a cupboard door and the sink is full.]

EXAMINER, read aloud word for word:
"Part two. In this part, I am going to show you a picture and ask you three questions. You will have one minute to think about your answers before you start speaking. You will have two minutes to answer all three questions. Begin speaking when you hear this sound (chime). Look at the photograph."

[Stage direction: the three questions below (7a, 7b, 7c) are all part of scored item 7 and are answered together. Read them aloud once, in order, before the preparation minute begins, and remind the candidate: "You do not need to describe the picture."]

QUESTION 7a - "Tell me about a daily habit or routine of yours that you have changed in the last few years. What did you change, and why?"

QUESTION 7b - "How has that change affected your own day and the people you live with?"

QUESTION 7c - "In general, what do you think has the strongest influence on the way people organise their daily lives - their work, their family, their money, or the technology they use?"

[Stage direction: start the 1 minute of preparation now; the candidate may make notes. After 60 seconds say "Your minute is up," sound the chime and start the 2 minutes. Give a quiet warning at 30 seconds remaining only if the candidate has fallen silent. Stop the candidate politely at 2 minutes, say "Thank you," and move on to Part three.]

parts.title: Part 3
parts.instructions:
CEFR Multilevel Mock - Speaking - Variant A (Everyday life, home and daily routine) | Part 3

Part 3 - Balanced argument on a topic statement (Housework and written schedules). CEFR C1. One topic statement with a FOR list of three points and an AGAINST list of three points. Choose TWO points from each list and give a balanced argument representing both sides. 1 minute of preparation, then 2 minutes of speaking. This is scored item 8 (0-6).

EXAMINER NOTE - OFFICIAL SCORING SPLIT:
items 1-3 (Part 1.1, scored together) = 0-5; items 4-6 (Part 1.2, scored together) = 0-5; item 7 (Part 2) = 0-5; item 8 (Part 3) = 0-6. Maximum raw score 21, converted to a rating out of 75.

OFFICIAL RAW SCORE -> RATING CONVERSION:
21=75, 20.5=73, 20=71, 19.5=69, 19=67, 18.5=65, 18=64, 17.5=63, 17=61, 16.5=59, 16=57, 15.5=56, 15=54, 14.5=52, 14=51, 13.5=50, 13=49, 12.5=47, 12=46, 11.5=45, 11=43, 10.5=42, 10=40, 9.5=39, 9=38, 8.5=37, 8=35, 7.5=33, 7=32, 6.5=30, 6=29, 5.5=27, 5=26, 4.5=24, 4=23, 3.5=21, 3=19, 2.5=17, 2=15, 1.5=13, 1=11, 0.5=10, 0=0

questions.q:
[PART 3 - CEFR C1 - scored item 8 - one topic statement with a FOR list and an AGAINST list]

EXAMINER, read aloud word for word:
"Part three. In this part, you are going to speak on a topic for two minutes. You can see the topic on the screen and two lists of points - for and against - related to the topic. Choose two items from each list and give a balanced argument to represent both sides of the topic. You have one minute to prepare your argument. You will then have two minutes to speak. Begin speaking when you hear this sound (chime)."

[Stage direction: show the statement and both lists on the screen, or read them aloud twice if no screen is available. Then give exactly 1 minute of silent preparation, sound the chime, and allow 2 minutes of speaking. Remind the candidate once before the preparation minute: "Choose two points from each list - not all of them."]

TOPIC STATEMENT:
"Housework in a shared home should be divided by a written schedule rather than left to whoever happens to notice it."

FOR (choose two):
 1. A written schedule makes each person's share visible, so nobody quietly ends up doing far more than the others.
 2. It removes the daily negotiation, and with it most of the arguments about who was supposed to do what.
 3. Young people in the household learn to plan and take responsibility for tasks they would otherwise avoid.

AGAINST (choose two):
 1. Real weeks are uneven - illness, exams and long shifts make a fixed rota unfair rather than fair.
 2. Running a home like a workplace can drain the goodwill that makes living together pleasant.
 3. People begin working to the list instead of to the result, doing a task badly just to tick it off.

[Stage direction: start the 1 minute of preparation now. After 60 seconds sound the chime and start the 2 minutes. If the candidate argues only one side, you may prompt once: "And the other side?" Stop the candidate politely at 2 minutes and say: "Thank you. That is the end of the test."]
